name: mint cilantro chicken
instructions:
Priya Krishna's Garlic-Ginger Chicken with Cilantro and Mint (Indian-ish, via her aunt Sonia) — NOW THE DEFAULT BUILD of this recipe, with a few modifications from experience (PURÉE the marinade, SLICE the chicken small, DON'T pour the marinade into the pan). Her original as printed is recorded in the notes. See [[jaffrey-mint-lentils]] for the sister recipe by herb pair — same mint+cilantro but built on a madhur jaffrey tarka-style dal.

=== INGREDIENTS (HER QUANTITIES, SERVES 4) ===

MARINADE:
- 8 garlic cloves
- 2 tbsp fresh ginger
- 1 tbsp fresh mint leaves, plus more for garnish
- 1 tbsp fresh cilantro leaves, plus more for garnish
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 3 tbsp fresh LEMON juice (from 1 lemon) — DON'T FORGET THE LEMON (see notes)
- 1 tbsp ground coriander (freshly ground is best)
- 1 tsp ground turmeric
- 1/2 tsp red chile powder
- 1 tsp AMCHUR (dry mango powder)
- 3/4 tsp kosher salt

CHICKEN:
- 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (1/2 to 3/4 lb each)
- 1 tsp olive oil for the pan

=== PROCEDURE (DEFAULT — HER RECIPE + MY MODIFICATIONS) ===

1. PURÉE THE MARINADE: blend the ginger, garlic, lemon juice, mint, and cilantro into a PURÉE (she hand-minces into a paste — but if you don't do the purée, you lose flavor). Mix in the salt and the spices (coriander, turmeric, red chile powder, amchur) and the olive oil.

2. CUT THE CHICKEN BREAST INTO SMALL SLICES — this is required, not optional: there is NO BRAISING STEP, so the chicken must be in small slices before it hits the skillet.

3. MARINADE: coat the sliced chicken in the purée (her method: resealable bag, massage it on, refrigerate 2 hours).

4. COOK: heat a skillet with a little olive oil. Add JUST THE SUBMERGED/WET CHICKEN to the pan — DO NOT POUR THE MARINADE MIXTURE IN with it. The oil and heat cause the mint to separate and turn an ugly green color (see notes). Cook the slices through.

5. Garnish with the reserved fresh mint and cilantro.
notes:
Priya Krishna's Garlic-Ginger Chicken with Cilantro and Mint is now the DEFAULT build, with my modifications (purée marinade, sliced chicken, no marinade in the pan). The pre-Priya spice-crust + herb-finish build this file used to carry is preserved below as the OLD BUILD.

=== HER ORIGINAL, AS PRINTED (INDIAN-ISH, P. 187) ===

Serves 4. Marinade: 8 garlic cloves minced; 2 tbsp minced fresh ginger; 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint + more for garnish; 1 tbsp finely chopped fresh cilantro + more for garnish; 3 tbsp olive oil; 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice (1 lemon); 1 tbsp ground coriander (freshly ground best); 1 tsp ground turmeric; 1/2 tsp red chile powder; 1 tsp amchur; 3/4 tsp kosher salt. Chicken: 4 boneless skinless breasts (1/2–3/4 lb each); 1 tsp olive oil.

1. MAKE THE MARINADE: in a medium bowl, mix the garlic, ginger, mint, cilantro, the 3 tbsp oil, and lemon juice into a paste.
2. In a small bowl, mix the coriander, turmeric, red chile powder, amchur, and salt, then add to the garlic-ginger paste and stir well. Transfer to a large resealable bag.
3. MAKE THE CHICKEN: place the breasts in the marinade, seal, massage to coat evenly. Refrigerate 2 hours.
4. Warm a large skillet over medium-high. Once quite hot, add the oil, swirl to coat. Reduce to medium, remove chicken from marinade, add to pan. Cook 1–2 min without moving until lightly golden, flip, 1–2 min more until golden on the second side. Reduce heat to LOW, COVER, cook 10 minutes (without peeking!). Turn off the heat (if you… [PAGE CUT OFF — the recipe continues on the next page; continuation not yet captured].

Her framing: both the marinade and the low-and-sort-of-slow cooking method are the point — charred, spicy, slightly funky, juicy chicken, good alone or rolled up in a roti taco-style with salads and chutneys.

=== PURÉE THE MARINADE — CORRECTING THE OLD RECORD ===

I LIKE BLENDING the ginger, garlic, lemon juice, mint, and cilantro into a PURÉE and using that to marinade the chicken with the salt and spices. IF YOU DON'T DO THE PURÉE, YOU LOSE FLAVOR.

(Record correction: an earlier version of these notes claimed Priya's original was a blender marinade and dispreferred it. Wrong on both counts — her printed original is a hand-minced paste, and the purée marinade is now the preferred move.)

=== DON'T POUR THE MARINADE INTO THE PAN ===

Marinading the chicken in the herb purée is right — but DO NOT pour the marinade mixture into the pan when you cook: the oil and heat cause the MINT to SEPARATE and become an UGLY GREEN color. Just the submerged/wet chicken goes on the pan.

=== SLICE THE CHICKEN SMALL — NO BRAISING STEP ===

Because there is no braising step, you MUST cut the chicken breast into small slices before they hit the skillet. (Her original cooks whole breasts with a covered low 10-minute finish; the sliced version doesn't get that.)

=== THE LEMON IS IMPORTANT ===

I used to forget the lemon. It helps with marinading a lot, and with flavor. Don't skip it.

=== AMCHUR — COOKED IN FROM THE MARINADE ===

Note she puts 1 tsp amchur in the marinade, cooked in with the chicken — a counterpoint to the amchur-as-finishing-dust-only placement in [[indian-street-chicken]] (tartness survives heat; it's the fruity top notes that fade).

=== CHICKEN NOTES ===

CHICKEN BREAST OVER THIGH: this recipe works better with chicken breast than thigh. Breast carries the spice-and-herb register cleanly; thigh's fattiness competes with the bright herb finish.

=== TOFU IS OUT — THE UNLOADED-CARRIER FAILURE ===

The tofu variant (fry the tofu, add the herb finish after) is REMOVED — it doesn't work. Fried tofu + raw mint/cilantro after is sad: the herb finish is lean and vegetal and needs the protein to bring flavor, which naked tofu doesn't. Tofu earns its place in indian cooking only LOADED — the yogurt-marinade-and-broil of [[tikka-masala]] (home-pressed firm), or a spiced fritter coat. Same lean-on-lean failure as tofu-in-palak ([[palak-paneer]] — paneer is the flavor).

=== THE CHILE STACK (FROM THE OLD BUILD — STILL AVAILABLE) ===

Her original uses only 1/2 tsp red chile powder. The old build's indian chile stack — generic chili powder + KASHMIRI chili powder (bright red color, gentle warmth, makes it visually indian) + RED CHILI FLAKES (whole-form accent) — same rule as [[palak-paneer]].

FRESH GREEN CHILE: a small amount adds bright whole-form heat the powders don't. SERRANOS preferable — slit lengthwise (1–2 slits) so heat leeches without the chile dissolving in; fish out at the end if desired. JALAPEÑOS work — dice them, use sparingly (1/4 jalapeño or less). Background heat, not chile-forward; if in doubt, err less.

=== BELL PEPPERS ARE CLASHING ===

Bell peppers (any color) don't fit — sweet-vegetal character fights the herb-forward mint + cilantro register and pushes toward generic stir-fry. The green chile slot handles pepper here.

=== OLD BUILD — SPICE-CRUST + HERB-FINISH-AT-THE-END (PRESERVED AS ALTERNATE) ===

Before adopting Priya's marinade as the default, this recipe was: chicken cooked in GHEE with a turmeric/chili powder/CUMIN/coriander spice crust, finished OFF HEAT with a raw mash of mint + cilantro + garlic + ginger + LIME. Herb-finish ladder for that build: (1) chop/mash and add to the pan at the very end, saag-style — the default; (2) mortar-pestle pesto-style paste — the refinement; (3) [[mint-cilantro-chimichurri]] (variant A, indian) as a side condiment ONLY on bread/naan — never spooned on the protein (reads as two dishes otherwise). Skip chimichurri without bread.

The don't-cook-the-herbs principle from that build survives in refined form: herbs AS MARINADE ON the chicken is fine (that's the default now); herbs poured INTO the hot pan as liquid is what breaks (mint separates, ugly green).

=== SERVING PAIRING — [[braised-turnips]] AS A SIDE ===

[[braised-turnips]] pairs particularly well — register-fit is right (mild, buttery, savory), neither dish crowds the other. ESPECIALLY with LEMON OR LIME JUICE added to the turnips at the glaze stage — the citrus finish echoes the citrus in the marinade and ties the plate together.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[jaffrey-mint-lentils]]: the split-out lentil sister recipe. Same mint + cilantro pair, completely different structure (madhur jaffrey tarka-style dal — whole spices bloomed in oil, onion+garlic+tomato base, whole green lentils, herbs stirred in raw at the end).
- [[mint-cilantro-chimichurri]]: raw mint+cilantro chimichurri (variant A — indian). Side-condiment option in the OLD BUILD, on bread/naan only.
- [[palak-paneer]]: shares the kashmiri + chili powder + red chili flakes stack.
- [[indian-street-chicken]]: the other amchur-on-chicken recipe — opposite amchur placement (finishing dust there, cooked-in marinade here).
- [[pesarattu]]: shares the serrano-as-fresh-chile approach.
original_chef: Priya Krishna — Indian-ish, 'Garlic-Ginger Chicken with Cilantro and Mint' (p. 187), the brainchild of her aunt Sonia.
